proof:
Translate $g$ to zero. If $A$ is the part of $K$ in a shifted strip of half-width $s$, then $(A+(-A))/2$ lies in the centered strip by convexity and symmetry. Its volume is at least $|A|$ by Brunn–Minkowski when $|A|>0$, and the desired bound is immediate when $|A|=0$.

For fixed $u$ write $T(b)=\mathbb P(u\cdot X\ge b)$. Projection hyperplanes are null and $T(-b)=1-T(b)$. For $a=u\cdot y\ge0$,
$$
T(a+t)+T(a-t)=1-\mathbb P(t-a\le u\cdot X\le t+a)\ge2T(a),
$$
with equality at $t=0$. For $a<0$ the sum is $1+\mathbb P(t+a\le u\cdot X\le t-a)\ge1$ and equals one when $|t|$ is sufficiently large by compactness. Either minimum, multiplied by $V$, is at least $2f_K(y)$, since each cap through $y$ has mass at least $f_K(y)$ and opposite caps through $y$ sum to $V$. Taking $t=0$ and then the infimum over $u$ gives the reverse bound.

For the convolution, condition on $Z$. In each direction the probability of the closed through-$y$ cap equals the expectation of $T(a-u\cdot Z)$ and, by symmetry of $Z$, of $T(a+u\cdot Z)$. Their average is at least $f_K(y)/V$ pointwise in the projected shift. This applies to every direction. A closed halfspace containing $y$ contains its parallel through-$y$ halfspace. No integrability of $Z$ is used.
statement: Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body, $d\ge1$, centrally symmetric about $g$, with volume $V$. For any $u\ne0$, $s\ge0$, and $b\in\mathbb R$, the volume of $K$ in the strip $|u\cdot(x-g)-b|\le s$ is at most its volume in $|u\cdot(x-g)|\le s$. For any $y\in\mathbb R^d$ and fixed $u\ne0$, the minimum over $t\in\mathbb R$ of the sum of the two cap volumes with thresholds $u\cdot y\pm t$ is twice the ordinary through-$y$ cap volume in direction $u$ if $u\cdot(y-g)\ge0$, attained at $t=0$, and $V$ otherwise, attained at all sufficiently large $|t|$. Thus the infimum over both $u$ and $t$ is $2f_K(y)$, where $f_K(y)$ is the ordinary raw halfspace depth at $y$. If $X$ is uniform on $K$ and $Z$ is independent of $X$ with $Z$ and $-Z$ identically distributed, then the normalized halfspace depth of $X+Z$ at each $y$ is at least $f_K(y)/V$.
title: Paired caps and symmetric convolution at every point of a symmetric convex body
